strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy issue #17787 / PR #22433: RectBivariateSpline with s>0 on large grids returns NaN everywhere on the buggy commit a65c459ea933. The project's new test test_spline_large_2d (parametrized over shapes (350,850),(2000,170) and s_tols) asserts no NaN and then checks closeness to z. Build SciPy from the buggy and fixed revisions, then run that test on each. Success is the transition: the NaN assertion fails on buggy and passes on fixed. Platform, memory state and build flags may decide whether the NaN appears at all, so the transition is not guaranteed.

build_commands: pip install -e . --no-build-isolation  (or: spin build, then run tests via spin test)
git checkout <fixed commit of PR 22433 merge> && rebuild with the same command
git checkout -- scipy/interpolate/tests/test_fitpack2.py  and apply the reproducing test diff onto both revisions before running
pinned_because: numpy version not stated in evidence; use the numpy the buggy commit's pyproject.toml requires (era-inferred, not documented)
build backend (meson-python) inferred from the modern scipy build layout, not stated in evidence
gfortran is required because fitpack (dfitpack.pyf, fpregr.f) is Fortran; this is documented by the code layout in the context

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/interpolate/tests/test_fitpack2.py::test_spline_large_2d (parametrized by shape and s_tols) and scipy/interpolate/tests/test_fitpack2.py::test_spline_large_2d_maxit (uses maxit=25 keyword)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy a65c459ea933 the test_spline_large_2d cases with s=1 and s=3 (and possibly s=0 on large shapes) fail at assert(not np.isnan(z_spl).any()) because the evaluated spline contains NaN; on the fixed revision these same cases pass, meaning no NaN and xp_assert_close succeeds within the stated atol/rtol. test_spline_large_2d_maxit fails on buggy with TypeError (unexpected keyword maxit), not with the NaN assertion, so it confirms only that the API is absent on buggy, not the numerical defect.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: array containing NaN values (np.isnan(spl(x, y)).any() is True)
input_output_examples.expected_output: no NaN values in the evaluated spline

risks: The NaN is described as irregular and dependent on memory state; a single run on buggy may not show it, so repeat runs or several shapes may be needed.
The reporter suspects memory allocation failure; if the failure needs a specific allocator or memory pressure, it will not reproduce on a normal development machine.
Test uses atol/rtol from s_tols; the exact tolerance at which correct and incorrect answers separate is not stated in the evidence.
Precision dependence (float32 vs float64) is not stated; the test casts to float64, so float32 behaviour is unverified.
test_spline_large_2d_maxit is skipped on 32-bit systems and segfaults there per the test reason; run on 64-bit only.
Tests are marked slow; if the runner skips slow tests by default, select them explicitly.
Buggy commit a65c459ea933 and PR date are not confirmed by the passages; the fixed revision commit hash is not provided and must be identified from PR 22433's merge.
Behaviour with maxit values other than the default 20 is only qualitative in the evidence.
If the platform is not Linux x86_64 with gfortran, the defect may not transition; a sanitizer build would not be expected to change the NaN outcome but has not been verified.

oracle.tolerance: atol/rtol from parametrized s_tols: (0,1e-12,1e-7), (1,7e-3,1e-4), (3,2e-2,1e-4); NaN check is exact
oracle.reference_source: input data z (the spline should approximate it for the given s)
oracle.why: The NaN assertion is exact; the closeness check uses the test's parametrized tolerances, which come from the developer test, not a stated separation threshold for the bug.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: assert(not np.isnan(z_spl).any()) sees True for np.isnan(...).any() because the evaluated spline contains NaN, so the assertion raises AssertionError before the closeness check runs.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The spline evaluates without NaN, so the NaN assertion passes, and xp_assert_close(z_spl, z, atol, rtol) passes for the parametrized tolerances.
